reviews.comment: Not the best at giving lectures, but also not the worst. Dr. Safonov's lectures give you a basic understanding of the material, but if you really want to do well I'd recommend reading the textbook and taking notes from there. Make sure you attend class because there's lots of iclicker questions. Oh yeah and he gives us like 5 seconds to answer.

He was out two lectures and we had another professor come in and teach and he made a lot of the class hate lectures with Safonov because they felt so useless. Safonov's lectures seemed way easier in comparison to the exams so you feel unprepared. They were slow and boring. I think he is a good person and genuinely cares, the structure was just bad.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Safonov is a very kind and supportive professor. The exams for Physics 206 are common exams across all sections, so the difficulty of the tests does not depend on the individual instructor. In terms of teaching, Dr. Safonov explains the material clearly and incorporates many helpful examples during lectures.

This guy is genius. The class is really hard, but he spends a lot of time doing harder practice problems in class, so when you get to the exam everything is kind of similar. He does exam reviews 2-3 days before exam days which I found really helpful.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: In my opinion, which 206 professor you get doesn't matter too much, because most of the learning comes from reading the textbook and doing the homework. Multiple times throughout the semester he would get halfway through a problem and realize he didn't know how to solve it. There are definitely better profs, like Dr. May.

Safonov is a brilliant physicist, but he is clearly a research professor and doesn't get assigned lectures very often. The first few weeks were rough, but he adjusted and became a fantastic lecturer by the end of the semester. Hes always available for help, and hosts very helpful extra review sessions the Friday night before each exam.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most of my issues with PHYS 206 were not Safonov's fault since this was a common course. For Safanov specifically, lectures were good and he worked examples out in a way that was easy to understand. My only complaint is that he focused a little too heavily on IClicker questions during class. Other classes has less questions with easier content.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Overall Dr. Safonov is a great professor for University Physics, he explains concepts very well and always has a lot of conceptual examples! However sometimes he can go off on tangents and work out problems that are very time consuming for our lecture. Great availability for office hours and exam reviews! Not a bad choice!

He's a very great lecturer, he provides alot of examples and explains concepts very understandably. Iclicker questions and examples are very similar to HW and exams. I will say he does sometimes spends a too long deriving equations, but he gives you a solid conceptual understanding of physics. Has office hours and review for exams! Solid Choice
Only reason I did good in this class was because of our TA. Lectures ae very boring and don't learn much from them, he depends on the book to teach you for the most part.

This professor is more there for the research and it is pretty obvious. He missed many weeks of school to go to research events. He was constantly canceling or rescheduling office hours to go to research events. I would recommend taking a different professor.

Safonov is a great professor. He doesn't move too fast or slow. He always answers questions even if they are stupid. I would highly recommend him for PHYS 206. You can really tell that he cares about his students and wants them to be successful.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Safonov is a good choice for Phys 206! He is always open for questions, and he is always willing to answer questions when asked.(No matter how stupid the question is ). Phys 206 is just a hard class regardless of who you take.. just dont take Bassichis. Mason, Tatiana, and Safonov should alway be your choices.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I didn't take Dr. Safonov for lecture but he would hold the review sessions for exams and from what I experienced with him, he really cares about you learning the material. He was willing to go overtime to help students understand and really welcomed any type of questions if anything was unclear. Great professor!

201 tests are common tests, so it doesn't matter who you take. He was caring, and wanted his students to do well. He worked problems with variables instead of numbers; most people stopped going to class. He's a competent prof, but I think success in this class comes from recitation and learning to work problems on your own. Final was curved a lot.

Safonov is one of the more difficult professors for 201. If you have the option, take one of the other professors. Make sure you do really well on the first test because it will only get much harder from there. He gives a pretty decent curve. My grades on test were: 73,48,45,30, and a 29 on the final and still ended up with a C in the class.

I had to Q-drop the course but honestly the tests looked nothing like what he lectured over. the third test had a 38% average. the tests are curved but barely. lectures were super boring but you have to pay attention. i hated the class.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great Professor which an understandable accent. He makes sure that you know the material and has given outside test prep to make sure you do well. He had one of the higher averages against other teachers. Gives plenty of material for test to study and makes sure you are aware of everything. Test are not his but are general PHYS 218 test

Safonov was a decent Physics 218 professor. Honestly, the class will be hard no matter what professor you take. I liked that he worked practice problems in class instead of just teaching concepts. He also encouraged students to ask questions. You need to read the textbook multiple times and understand all the homework to do well in this class.

Has an accent, but not too difficult to understand. Does a good job teaching the material. Tests are difficult, but doable if you study. If you put in the effort, it is definitely possible to get an A.

Safonov is an advocate of tough love, he teaches you what you need to know in lecture but he makes you work for the grade. He was good at explaining concepts and answering questions. He is a difficult grader but only because you should know how to do it. Don't take him if you don't expect to work for it!
The tests are really difficult and he does a poor job of explaining his work on a problem during lecture. He gives off the vibe of not caring if he makes a lot of students fail.

DO NOT TAKE HIM.  His tests are ridiculous. He would show up late and not give us the entire class to finish him.  He was very rude during office hours, and did not seem very interested in making sure we learned the material.  I would never take a class with him again.

If you want to do well on the tests, read the chapter, know the concepts, and DO THE PICTURE PROBLEMS IN THE EXERCISES FROM THE CHAPTER! He always uses book problems on the test, always. And they are always the picture diagram ones.
Says his goal is to make students fail. He is very intelligent but he definitely teaches too quick.
Good prof, uses good examples in class, gives out candy for asking good questions in class

If you have a good foundation in physics you should be fine but if you're like me who had a terrible high school physics teacher, it can be hard to catch up as Safanov tends to go pretty quickly through the material and it's easy to miss concepts or not understand what's going on.
It is a tough teacher but he clearly demonstrates what he is doing and gives you step by step instructions. The homework isn't bad but the tests are pretty tough. He is a good prof.

He is TOUGH but he is better than some other professors that I have heard about.  Try to get Professor White and if you can not get him get Professor Safanov.  4 tests. Online homework (mastering physics) that you have to get a 70 or higher on or you fail, but these are extremely easy, my lowest grade is like a 92, easy if you work in groups.
